name: scaling-benchmarks
title: Scaling benchmarks: how decomposition scales with model size and instance count
question:
How does the decomposition cost scale with model size, and how much parallel
speedup does the same-rate ensemble buy as instance count grows — and what is
the committed performance baseline the Rust-engine spike (Phase 6) is measured
against?
hypothesis:
The same-rate ensemble gives a real wall-clock speedup that grows with instance
count (a parallel win). Decomposition is NOT a free win on model size: its
per-tick orchestration makes it slower end-to-end than the monolith at the sizes
an affordable sweep reaches; the monolithic libroadrunner BUILD only strains
superlinearly at large N (established separately). These numbers, on this
machine, are the Phase-6 baseline.
objective:
Run a bounded systematic sweep — monolithic vs decomposed wall-clock vs species
count (multiorgan_scaling) and ensemble serial-vs-parallel speedup vs instance
count (ensemble_speedup) — record it as a machine-tagged baseline, and grade the
robust, machine-independent properties.
description:
Performance study for the SBML-decomposition investigation. The scaling harness
(viva_sbml_decomposition.harness.scaling) reuses `multiorgan_scaling` (model-size
curve) and `ensemble_speedup` (instance scaling, Ray with serial fallback).

Wall-clock is NOT reproducible across machines/BLAS/load, so the verdict grades
only robust properties: the ensemble gives a parallel speedup > 1 (measured up to
~7.5x at P=8 on this machine, matching ensemble-and-multirate), and decomposition
is slower end-to-end than the monolith at the measured sizes (the investigation's
honest "decomposition is not free"). The monolithic-build exponent is RECORDED as
the baseline (~0.9 over a small species range; the superlinear O(N^1.64) strain is
a large-N regime measured in bigger-models-and-abm-limit, cited not re-proved).
The committed baseline (visualizations/scaling_benchmarks.json) is this machine's
numbers and is the reference Phase 6 compares viva-core against.

expected_behavior.name: ensemble-parallel-speedup
expected_behavior.observable: same-rate ensemble serial vs parallel (Ray) wall-clock speedup vs instance count
expected_behavior.condition: parallel speedup > 1 when a parallel backend runs (serial fallback is caveated, not a failure)
expected_behavior.rationale: independent instances are embarrassingly parallel, so a real OS-process parallel backend must beat serial.

expected_behavior.name: decomposition-cost-characterized
expected_behavior.observable: monolithic vs decomposed end-to-end wall-clock vs species count, and the monolithic-build exponent
expected_behavior.condition: decomposition is slower end-to-end than the monolith at the measured sizes (not a free win); the build exponent is recorded as the baseline
expected_behavior.rationale: decomposition buys composability, not speed, at affordable sizes; the superlinear build strain is a large-N regime established elsewhere.
